$comment: Reviewer identities for zheref/kro-pwa, read by `nen pr ready` (CON-32). Declared as DATA so the readiness verdict is deterministic for every pull request: without this file nen refuses to judge rather than guess a reviewer set. This is a single-maintainer consumer repository: the human merge at G2 is the real approval and stays outside the automated verdict. REWORKED 2026-10-12 to the shape zheref/KroApple adopted under the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-05: Copilot and Cursor Bugbot ran out of review credits, so the base reviewer is the `hanten` check (.github/workflows/hanten.yml + scripts/hanten_gate.sh) and no AI bot round is owed; both bots stay declared so a round either does post is recognised and its threads still bind.

reviewers.$comment: Posts as copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]. Reviews once when the PR opens when it has credits; nothing re-requests it after a push, so under the bounded policy only a PENDING request owes a round. Not in `base_reviewers` since 2026-10-12 (credits exhausted); a round it does post is still recognised and its threads must be resolved (CON-32(d)).
reviewers.name: copilot

reviewers.$comment: Cursor Bugbot posts under a login carrying either word and its check name varies with the installation -- an unanchored, case-insensitive substring. It enrols only when its own check is present at the head (optional, but binding once it shows up) and is `bounded_policy_exempt` (maintainer ruling 2026-09-25): Cursor bills per review and can run out of credits mid-effort, so an enrolled bugbot owes a round only while a request for one is pending -- a missing bugbot is silence, not a blocker; a bugbot that spoke is binding.
reviewers.name: bugbot

reviewers.$comment: The hanten round, as a check (maintainer ruling 2026-10-05, adopted here 2026-10-12). Copilot and Cursor Bugbot both ran out of review credits, so no AI bot round can be what CON-32(b) waits on. `hanten` is the one base reviewer instead: its round is the `hanten` job of .github/workflows/hanten.yml, which runs scripts/hanten_gate.sh against the pull request body and concludes SUCCESS only when the `## Adversarial review (hanten)` section is present, every row of its findings table is fixed, pushed-back or deferred, and the checklist ticks `Adversarial review settled`. The job re-runs on `edited`, so settling a finding in the body re-reads the round. The login pattern is anchored to a name no reviewer posts under: the check is the round, never a review.
reviewers.name: hanten

reviewers.$comment: The maintainer. The human merge at G2 is the real approval; this row exists so a review the maintainer posts is recognised. Not a default approver under `review-round-only`: an APPROVED review is not required for readiness, the merge decision itself is the approval.
reviewers.name: zheref

$approval: POLICY. `review-round-only` with no default approvers matches zheref/hatsu's and zheref/KroApple's gates.json and the maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-12: the automated review round is what readiness waits on, a separate APPROVED review is not required, and the human merge decision stays outside the automated verdict.
$base_reviewers: RULING 2026-10-05 (zheref/KroApple), adopted here 2026-10-12: the base set is `hanten` alone, and no minimum round is expected from any AI bot reviewer. Copilot and bugbot stay declared, so a round either one does post is recognised and its threads still have to be resolved (CON-32(d) reads every thread whatever the reviewer set), but neither is in the base set, so neither owes anything, and the ruleset's automatic Copilot request, which a credit-exhausted Copilot never answers, cannot stall the gate. Copilot has no enrolment check, so a request for it enrols nothing; bugbot enrols only when its own check is present, and as `bounded_policy_exempt` it then owes a round only while a request for one is pending. The schema refuses an empty base set, which is why hanten's check stands in rather than the set simply being emptied. Revert to ["copilot"] when its credits return, if the maintainer wants the bot round back.
$round_policy: Reviewer-round caps by default (ruling 2026-09-30): at most two requested bot rounds per pull request. nen reads `maxRounds` from 0.21 (`pr request-reviews` refuses a request past it); at the 0.20 pin the key is preserved as data.

delivery.$comment: What a delivery (integration) pull request looks like here. No delivery bot exists in this repository, so the author pattern matches nobody; the `integration/` head prefix is the one real signal -- the landing-page effort of 2026-10-12 is the first integration branch (integration/landing-page), opened by the maintainer's own credentials.
